display.title: Episode 425: Hillel on the Roof (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: A Sefirah show: why we learn Pirkei Avos before Shavuos, Shema with a young yeshiva student, the story of Hillel listening to the Torah lesson from a snowy skylight, and Lag BaOmer plans.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens in the middle of the days of Sefirah. Just as the Jewish people counted the days from leaving Egypt to receiving the Torah, every year we feel a new love for Torah, and we learn a chapter of Pirkei Avos each Shabbos afternoon, because good midos must come before Torah. A nine-year-old yeshiva student leads the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time tells of Hillel, who could not afford the time to chop firewood for the shul, so he lay on the skylight in a blizzard to hear the lesson below. Found frozen under the snow, he is carried inside and revives, and the townspeople free him from bringing wood. He grows up to be the great Hillel of the Mishnah and Pirkei Avos. Next, a third-grade girls' class sings the Four Questions to an old-world tune. The show ends with the meaning of Lag BaOmer and the yahrzeit of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, an invitation to the Tzivos Hashem Lag BaOmer parade and carnival, help choosing a Torah-true summer camp, and Shabbos candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: True love for Torah means being ready to give up comfort, and even more, to learn; we prepare to receive the Torah by improving our midos.

quality.notes: The Sefirah talk and the Hillel story also aired in episode 375 (May 1989), so this show reuses that material with new 1990 announcements. A short spoken fragment ('From all your children and grandchildren...') follows the song at 24:50, possibly a splice. Parade, camp line and candle times are period pieces.
